content.text: Sponsored Video Sponsored by Advertising Partner Watch to learn more Meaning of blockade in English blockadenoun [ C ] us Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /blɑːˈkeɪd/ uk Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /blɒkˈeɪd/ Add to word list Add to word list the situation in which a country or place is surrounded by soldiers or ships to stop people or goods from going in or out: an air and sea blockade The Soviet blockade of Berlin was lifted in May 1949. There is still some hope that the economic blockade will work and make military intervention unnecessary. Attacking & invading advance guard aggressor ambush beleaguer beleaguered besiege blitz false flag fire at someone/something full-frontal assault full-frontal attack going-over hit and run outflank pincer movement post-attack post-conquest pre-conquest surgical strike swoop See more results » blockadeverb [ T ] us Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /blɑːˈkeɪd/ uk Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /blɒkˈeɪd/ to surround a country or place with soldiers, ships, etc. to stop people or goods from going in or out: The Estonian port of Tallinn was blockaded for a time by Soviet warships. Fishermen began blockading ports to protest the high cost of diesel fuel. The army blockaded all roads in and out of the region.Protesters have blockaded airports to prevent the president from traveling.Farmers blockaded oil depots or drove their tractors slowly through the streets of cities. (Definition of blockade from the Cambridge Academic Content Dictionary © Cambridge University Press) blockade | Business English blockadenoun [ C ] POLITICS uk Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /blɒkˈeɪd/ us Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio Add to word list Add to word list a situation in which a group of people prevent goods or people entering or leaving a place as a way of showing a government or large organization that they do not agree with its decisions: The blockade of oil refineries caused fuel prices to double.impose/lift a blockade French farmers lifted their blockade of the Channel Tunnel yesterday. a situation in which one country refuses to trade with another country: It has defended the economic blockade despite mounting international criticism. blockadeverb [ T ] POLITICS uk Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /blɒkˈeɪd/ us Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio to prevent goods or people entering or leaving a place, especially as a way of showing disagreement with a government or large organization: Protesters are threatening to blockade refineries if the Government does not lower the tax on fuel. 0 seconds of 0 secondsVolume 0%Press shift question mark to access a list of keyboard shortcutsKeyboard ShortcutsEnabledDisabledPlay/PauseSPACEIncrease Volume↑Decrease Volume↓Seek Forward→Seek Backward←Captions On/OffcFullscreen/Exit FullscreenfMute/UnmutemSeek %0-9Live00:0000:0000:00 (Definition of blockade from the Cambridge Business English Dictionary © Cambridge University Press) Examples of blockade blockade It can be changed by lifting the blockade and ending the occupation. From Foreign Policy The blockade ended his possibilities to trade and sustain his family. From Foreign Policy That same year, some members of the community blockaded a road to a nearby diamond mine. From NPR Obstacles this way, blockades that way, and bridges burnt behind. From The New Yorker The government and eyewitnesses disagree about how the blockade ended. From CNN Ranch trucks occasionally drove by, but the few reporters outside the blockade were told no one was being let in. From OregonLive.com The group said it found hundreds of people in famine-like conditions it blamed on government blockades preventing food and supplies from entering. From USA TODAY The authorities also realized that hard-line measures and broadcast blockades would only worsen their position and that they must take their critics into account. From Foreign Policy The official information blockade only contributed to the protest mood. From Foreign Policy Other demonstrations are planned in other parts of the city, but the blockades that crippled traffic yesterday have now receded. From The Verge In the next step, the researchers investigated the blockade mechanism on more complex models, including a large protein fragment, similar to previous experiments. From Phys.Org In its wake, the massive blockades like those during 1991 became a thing of the past. From The Denver Post We will continue our fight against the financial blockade, and we will continue to publish. From Huffington Post Some legal scholars, however, view the aged and restrictive laws governing blockades as being out of step with modern conflict. From Slate Magazine Leaving aside the larger question of the blockade's legitimacy, the entire episode could have been handled without drama.
